---
title: "Second half – Exploration and replication"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this half](../../slides/housing-short.html#/half-2-exploration-and-replication){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

In the first half everyone who chose the same analyst reproduced the same number, because everyone ran the same code. In the second you become the sixth analyst and make choices of your own: you try a few analyses from the menu in the browser lab, read where the one that you would defend sits among every justifiable specification on these data, and end on the new audit that tested the claim again. Nothing is sent anywhere.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Specification menu](../../cases/housing/menu.qmd) and slides | The eleven decisions at three levels, the five on which the curve keeps more than one option, the 64 specifications that they make, and the ground rules for the menu; then a difference in proportions, and the linear probability model against the logit. | 14 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-4-menu) Task 4 | Call `try_spec()` with no arguments for the reference specification, then two or three times more, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `model = "three_group"`, to read why it is refused. Then rerun the one that you would defend, so that it is your last try. Skip `submit_exploration()`: the session sends nothing to the class chart. | 20 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) and slides | Your own small multiverse, and the curve of the claim, with the published result of the original authors (OAs) and the five analysts placed on it. An optional pair of slides tells where the idea of a multiverse came from. | 8 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-4-menu) | Rerun `try_spec()` with the specification that you would defend and read your placement, the number of the 64 specifications whose gap lies further below zero than yours, and send it in chat when the facilitator says go. | 5 minutes |
| Slides | What moved the estimate: each option of the curve set beside its twins, and the step in the curve that comes from the choice of which emails to count. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, with [the replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) on the case study as the follow-up | The SCORE replication, a preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities with new names; what it found; the original study and the replication compared row by row; the power of the two designs; the three Rs on this paper; and what separates robustness from replicability. | 13 minutes |
| Slides | Two points from the literature, the single analytical path, what you take with you, and the feedback form. | 7 minutes |

**By the end of the half** you have tried two or three alternatives one argument at a time, read the place of the one that you would defend among the 64 specifications of the curve, and met a claim that holds under every analysis of one sample and still failed on new data.
